q: AI coding agents increasingly obtain their behavior from artifacts outside the model: repository instructions, reusable skills, lifecycle hooks, commands, MCP server declarations, and subagent definitions.
r: IC1: static security and conformance audit of agent configuration declarations, no effect on cost or quality of coding agents and no evaluation of agents.

q: Skill maintenance in these public repositories is frequent, human-governed in the specific sense that every edit is authored or merged through a named human account
r: IC1: mining of how skill files are maintained for general lifelong agents, not coding agents and no effect on coding cost or quality.

q: We introduce RepoNorm to acquire explicit and implicit repository norms independently of coding tasks.
r: Include: acquires repository norms delivered as guidance to existing coding agents and measures effect on norm compliance, functional success and token cost (context mechanism, group b).

q: Across 1.53 million English skills, about one in seventeen (about 88,000) contains a directive that loosens that control
r: IC1: measures prevalence of oversight-loosening directives in skills for agents in general, a safety question with no coding-agent cost or quality outcome.

q: This paper is an experience report and an operating model, not an empirical validation
r: EC3: position and experience essay with no empirical evaluation of coding agents or context files.

q: The first measures how file size affects compliance and value.
r: IC1: theoretical model of instruction-file curation tested on instruction-following writing tasks (ManyIFEval) and simulations, no coding agent or software task.

q: We focus on scientific tasks whose outputs are executable Python programs evaluated in a sandbox.
r: IC1: test-time experience representations (skills vs genes) for general LLM agents on scientific scripting tasks, not software development with coding agents.

q: Repository-scale coding depends on an edit-time working set of coupled facts.
r: Include: controlled multi-trial study of repository-level coding agents across harnesses and models, with token-cost and instrumentation findings and a result on stale convention files.
